name: Space Complexity
description: Space complexity measures the extra memory an algorithm uses beyond the input, as a function of input size N. It includes auxiliary data structures, recursion call stacks, and output storage depending on the question's framing.
key_points: Auxiliary space: hash maps, arrays, sets created by the algorithm.
Recursion depth contributes to space — a DFS on a linked list can use O(N) stack space.
In-place algorithms use O(1) extra space.
Output space (e.g. storing all subsets) is often counted separately and can dominate.
examples: Hash map of N elements — O(N)
Recursion depth log N (balanced) vs N (skewed) — O(log N) vs O(N)
common_mistakes: Forgetting to count the recursion stack.
Claiming O(1) space when a copy of the input is created.
